_comment: The onboarding tour and the hub's first-week checklist (src/ui/tour.js). Copy only: the anchors are CSS selectors tried in order (a [data-tour] attribute first, so a page can name its own anchor), and every checklist tick is DERIVED from the open film in tour.js by the item's id — nothing here, and nothing about a tick, is stored. Only the tour's own place (which step, dismissed) is kept, in fms_tour_v1, and only when the reader clicks.

steps.title: Start with a real film
steps.body: The Dragon sample is a complete production — a screenplay, its scenes broken down, a schedule, a unit list and call sheets. Open it and every page of the studio has something on it to read, edit or delete.
steps.doneBody: The sample is open. Next, the story it was built from.

steps.title: Story: the idea, the logline, the beats
steps.body: Write the synopsis and tag its passages to the beats of a structure; the heatmap and the pacing notes are worked out from what you tag. The pitch deck is printed from here.

steps.title: Write: the screenplay
steps.body: It formats as you type — slug lines, action, cues, dialogue — and keeps the page count honest. Every scene heading you write becomes a scene in the breakdown.

steps.title: Breakdown: what each scene needs
steps.body: Tag cast, props, vehicles and sound against each scene. The elements list, the schedule, the budget and the call sheets all read these tags, so nothing is typed twice.

steps.title: Stripboard: scenes into shoot days
steps.body: Drag the strips into days. The day out of days, the calendar and the call sheets follow the board.

steps.title: Budget: what the schedule costs
steps.body: The estimate reads the days off your stripboard and the rates off the Chennai tables, and every figure stays editable. Change a shoot day and the number here follows it.
steps.doneBody: That is the plan priced. Next, the people it needs.

steps.title: Call sheets: who, where, when
steps.body: A call sheet is a day's scenes plus the people called for them. Print one, or save it as a PDF to send to the unit.

steps.title: Shoot day: on the phone, on the set
steps.body: Today's scenes, biggest first, with who is called. Mark each one shot, part or dropped; the edit log reads those marks to say what is in the can and what is still owed.
steps.doneBody: Marked. The edit log reads those marks next.

steps.title: Edit log: what is in the can
steps.body: The cut’s word on each scene, read from the marks you made on the floor. The set’s answer is final here — this page never writes back to a shoot day.
steps.doneBody: Now the last question: what actually leaves.

steps.title: Deliverables: what leaves, and where it goes
steps.body: Picture, sound, text and legal, each with what a festival or a streamer asks for. The festival list carries the date each entry was last checked, so you can see what is stale.
